subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the name of the cabinet in a synagogue that holds the Torah scrolls?
questions.explain: The Aron Hakodesh, or Holy Ark, is the cabinet on the eastern wall that holds the Torah scrolls.

questions.q: The raised platform from which the Torah is read to the congregation is called the:
questions.explain: The bimah is the raised reading desk or platform from which the Torah scroll is read.

questions.q: The seven-branched candlestick that is a traditional symbol of Judaism is the:
questions.explain: The menorah is a seven-branched candlestick and one of the oldest symbols of Judaism.

questions.q: The Jewish prayer book used in synagogue services is called the:
questions.explain: The siddur is the ordered prayer book containing the daily and Shabbat services.

questions.q: A minyan, the quorum required for public (communal) prayer, is a minimum of how many adults?
questions.explain: A minyan of ten adults is required before certain communal prayers and the public Torah reading may take place.

questions.q: Which prayer is the central Jewish declaration of faith, beginning 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One'?
questions.explain: The Shema, taken from Deuteronomy, is the central declaration of belief in the one God.

questions.q: The fringed prayer shawl worn by many Jews during prayer is the:
questions.explain: The tallit is a prayer shawl with fringes (tzitzit) at its corners, worn during prayer.

questions.q: The two plaited loaves of bread placed on the table for the Shabbat meal are called:
questions.explain: Two loaves of challah are used, recalling the double portion of manna provided before the Sabbath.

questions.q: What does the Ner Tamid, the light that burns continually above the Ark, represent?
questions.explain: The Ner Tamid ('eternal light') is never allowed to go out and symbolises God's everlasting presence.

questions.q: Why is the Ark usually placed on the wall of the synagogue that faces Jerusalem?
options: So that worshippers face the holy city when they pray
Because it keeps the scrolls cool
questions.explain: The Ark is set on the wall facing Jerusalem so the congregation prays towards the holy city and the site of the Temple.

questions.q: In an Orthodox synagogue, how are men and women usually seated during worship?
options: Separately, often with women in a gallery or separate section
Only men are allowed to enter
questions.explain: Orthodox synagogues seat men and women separately, whereas Reform synagogues allow mixed seating.

questions.q: Why is the Amidah traditionally recited while standing and facing Jerusalem?
options: It is a solemn prayer addressed directly to God, showing reverence
It is sung loudly by the whole congregation
It is only recited by children
It signals the beginning of Shabbat
questions.explain: The Amidah ('standing prayer') is said standing and facing Jerusalem to show reverence when addressing God.

questions.q: What is the main role of the chazzan (cantor) in a synagogue service?
options: To lead the congregation in the sung and chanted prayers
To light the Ner Tamid each day
questions.explain: The chazzan leads the congregation musically, chanting the liturgy on their behalf.

questions.q: Why do many Jewish men cover their head with a kippah during prayer?
options: To show respect and awareness of God above them
To keep warm inside the synagogue
Because the Torah may not be seen
questions.explain: Covering the head with a kippah expresses respect and reminds the wearer of God above them.

questions.q: Shabbat is kept as a day of rest mainly because, according to the Torah:
options: God rested on the seventh day after creating the world
It marks the Jewish New Year
It is the day the Torah was given
The Temple was destroyed on that day
questions.explain: Shabbat follows the pattern of creation, in which God rested on the seventh day and made it holy.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Havdalah ceremony?
options: To mark the end of Shabbat and separate it from the ordinary week
To begin Shabbat on Friday evening
To read the weekly Torah portion
questions.explain: Havdalah, using wine, spices and a plaited candle, marks the close of Shabbat and its separation from the weekdays.

questions.q: A visitor to a synagogue notices a lamp above the Ark that is never switched off. This lamp most likely represents:
questions.explain: This is the Ner Tamid, the eternal light, which symbolises the everlasting presence of God.

questions.q: Nine adults have gathered at a synagogue and wish to hold a full communal service including the public Torah reading. According to Orthodox practice they:
options: Cannot begin public prayer until a tenth person forms a minyan
May begin the full service straight away
Must wait until the next Shabbat
questions.explain: A minyan of ten is needed for communal prayer and the public Torah reading, so a tenth person is required.

questions.q: On Friday, just before sunset, a woman lights two candles in her home. She is marking the beginning of:
questions.explain: Lighting two candles before sunset on Friday welcomes in Shabbat in the Jewish home.

questions.q: During Shabbat a family does not switch on the oven, drive the car, or do household chores. This is because Shabbat is observed as:
options: A day of rest on which work is avoided
questions.explain: Shabbat is a day of rest in which the categories of work are set aside to keep the day holy.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Judaism: Worship
